title: Remote GPU capacity watch - RunPod deploy-when-available, network volumes, Vast.ai
description:
WATCH / RESEARCH - no code today. Two RunPod announcements (18 Jun 2026 'Deploy when available is now GA'; 03 Jun 2026 network-volume availability crunch). (1) Deploy-When-Available is CONSOLE-ONLY as of 2026-07-25 - verified against the live REST schema: POST /pods has no queue/schedule/subscription field, and we create via REST plus the GraphQL podFindAndDeployOnDemand fallback, so there is nothing to hook. We already ship the app-side equivalent (autoRetry, MPI-110). Revisit ONLY when the field appears in the REST or GraphQL schema; theirs is a real server-side reservation and beats our client-side poll, but it bills the instant capacity appears even with the app closed, so it must land behind the subscription window plus explicit consent - never folded silently into autoRetry. (2) RunPod publicly steered users off network volumes and ruled out credits for volume-availability pain; our remote engine is volume-pinned (volume locked to one DC, Connect gated on GPU plus volume). Escape hatch already exists (weights on R2 plus ephemeral Any-region pods, MPI-78, hot-store MPI-329) - this card is the trigger to measure it, not to build it. Full detail in brief.md.

MERGED 2026-08-01: this card absorbs MPI-344 (Vast.ai as a second option to runpod).
- MPI-344 - second provider option beside RunPod.
WHY ONE CARD: Both are watch/research on the same question - how the app gets a GPU when RunPod cannot give it one. Deploy-when-available, the network-volume availability crunch and a second provider are three answers to that question and get decided together, not one at a time.
The absorbed card(s) are closed as done/rejected - not built, kept as the record - and their full original text stays on disk at tasks/<id>/.
